interest: Japanese agitation in Ceylon and a naval survey disguised as poaching off Burma.
overview: This file (U.S. State Department decimal file 894.20246C) compiles diplomatic despatches and internal memoranda from 1935 and 1936 concerning Japanese subversive activities, propaganda, and maritime espionage in Ceylon and the surrounding Indian Ocean region. Reporting from Colombo, American Consul Robert L. Buell transmits detailed intelligence obtained from the British Naval Intelligence Officer of the East Indies Station regarding Japanese efforts to promote Pan-Asianism, cultivate ties with anti-British Sinhalese and Buddhist leaders, and challenge British imperial influence. The file also documents a significant hydrographic espionage incident in January 1936 off southern Burma, where a Royal Indian Navy vessel intercepted the Japanese motor vessel Taikya Maru, capturing an active Japanese naval officer and crew who were secretly taking soundings and scouting potential anchorages.

subfiles.about: A consular despatch reporting Japanese Pan-Asian propaganda, intelligence gathering, and cultivation of Buddhist and anti-British networks in Ceylon.
subfiles.from: Robert L. Buell, American Consul, Colombo, Ceylon
subfiles.summary: Consul Buell forwards intelligence received from the British Naval Intelligence Officer of the East Indies Station detailing Japanese subversive and propaganda efforts in Ceylon. He contrasts the previous popular, pro-Western consul, Mr. Kuroki—who was recalled after being criticized by a visiting Japanese vice-admiral for fraternizing with Europeans—with his successor, Mr. Ototsu, who immediately cultivated contacts among anti-British Sinhalese and Buddhist leaders. Ototsu promoted Japanese Buddhist affinity, arranged student trips to Japan, unsuccessfully sought to place a Japanese flag on the sacred tooth relic of Buddha in Kandy, and inspired newspaper opposition to local defense expenditures. The report also mentions an incident involving a prominent Japanese Buddhist priest who was refused entry after being caught with pornography rather than suspected propaganda materials.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 360: Japanese Subversive Activities in Ceylon

subfiles.about: An internal State Department memorandum summarizing the capture of a Japanese sounding vessel and naval officer off the southern coast of Burma.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: FE memo: Royal Indian Navy seized a Japanese vessel poaching and taking soundings off Burma, commanded by a naval officer.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Apprehension of Japanese Poaching and Survey Vessel off Burma

subfiles.about: A consular despatch detailing the interception, arrest, and trial of a Japanese hydrographic survey vessel operating off the southern coast of Burma.
subfiles.from: Robert L. Buell, American Consul, Colombo, Ceylon
subfiles.summary: Buell reports the seizure of the Taikya Maru off Mergui in January 1936, commanded by a Japanese naval officer taking soundings; the crew was interned at Singapore.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 454: Apprehension of Japanese Poachers
